subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw solve this by RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI access, a gateway single-writer lease, or both for `openclaw.sqlite` while a gateway is running?
rationale: Source confirms mutable CLI-side shared DB open and checkpoint paths, but the durable fix changes ownership across gateway observability, doctor migration, plugin-state diagnostics, and operator recovery.

options.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Route health/status/stability through the running gateway first and make fallback file opens read-only with no journal, checkpoint, or doctor-migration side effects while a gateway is active.

options.title: Gateway single-writer lease
options.body: Have the gateway own the state DB write/maintenance lease and make non-gateway processes fail closed or route through gateway APIs for writes and maintenance.

options.title: Forensic harness before implementation
options.body: Pause code changes until the reporter's corrupt DB bundle and a native runtime harness identify the exact OpenClaw helper/runtime interaction.

recommendation.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Route health/status/stability through the running gateway first and make fallback file opens read-only with no journal, checkpoint, or doctor-migration side effects while a gateway is active.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across the DB-first runtime-state architecture introduced through PR #78595 and the current gateway/CLI ownership model.
